observed_changes: status 'Order canceled and reimbursement issued.' appeared
Order actions collapsed to 'This order has no actions requiring your attention.'

visible_constraints: button 'Request refund' co-visible with 'Cancel order' on a paid order
Catalog documents refund as request -> complete chain; completeRefund gate present in availableActions

roles.name: anonymous
roles.note: No login, session cookie, bearer token, CSRF token, or other credential appeared in the recording. scope.json does not set authentication_required: true, so authentication is unknown/out of scope, NOT a missing-auth vulnerability. All state-changing endpoints are reachable without credentials.

observed_ui_rules.statement: After the order is canceled, all customer order actions are removed: the UI shows 'This order has no actions requiring your attention.' and the Request refund and Cancel order controls disappear.

facts.text: paragraph : This order has no actions requiring your attention.

inference.text: The UI intends a canceled order to be terminal and to expose no further customer actions; the server is expected to enforce this server-side, not only via the removed buttons.

observed_ui_rules.statement: The cancel action offers a single, fixed $100.00 reimbursement to the original payment method.

facts.text: paragraph : A $100.00 reimbursement will be sent to the original payment method.

inference.text: The UI presents one fixed reimbursement amount; the server should not trust a client-supplied reimbursement amount different from the order's original amount.

observed_ui_rules.statement: Price protection is not available while another order request is active; the price-adjustment action is removed after cancellation.

facts.text: paragraph : Price protection is not available while another order request is active.

inference.text: The UI intends price protection to be locked while another order request (such as cancellation) is active; the server should reject a price adjustment once the order is canceled or another request is in flight.

conflicting_action_pairs.state: delivered, paid order with requestRefund/requestPriceAdjustment/cancelOrder all true
conflicting_action_pairs.rule: Cancellation reimbursement, price protection adjustment, and refund completion must not stack into more than the original amount for the same order.

conflicting_action_pairs.rule: Price protection adjustment and refund completion must not stack into more than the original amount for the same order.

critical_endpoints.why: Payout-completion action: issues a cancellation reimbursement and sets totalReturned. Agent inference (unverified): with no auth, a client-supplied reimbursementAmount body field (the UI sends none) or a replay after the order is already canceled could overpay or double-pay; the raw observation is a bodyless POST that returned totalReturned=100 (== originalAmount), so the payout bound totalReturned<=originalAmount is the invariant to enforce.

Inferred from catalog + the 'Request refund' button; begins the refund payout chain. Agent inference (unverified): a client-supplied requestedAmount higher than the original order total could set up an oversized payout.

Inferred from catalog refund workflow (request -> complete); payout-completion action. Agent inference (unverified): because no auth is present, completing a refund without a prior request (or against an already-canceled/reimbursed order) could stack a second payout on top of the cancellation reimbursement, pushing totalReturned above originalAmount.

Inferred from catalog + the 'Request price adjustment' button (Eligible, $30.00 adjustment). Payout action that adds an adjustment to totalReturned. Agent inference (unverified): issuing it after cancellation, or racing it with cancel/refund completion, could stack a $30 adjustment on top of a $100 reimbursement and exceed originalAmount.
State reader used for before/after captures; exposes totalReturned, originalAmount, availableActions and payout sub-objects. Read-only; not an attack target but required to verify invariants.
